extracted.intended_audience: Researchers preparing manuscripts reporting in vivo (animal) experiments; journal editors and peer reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for authors on the minimum and recommended information to report when writing manuscripts of in vivo animal experiments, to allow assessment, replication and interpretation of study reliability and validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study design
rubrics_metrics.description: For each experiment, provide brief details of the study design including the groups being compared (including control groups) and identification of the experimental unit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the groups compared and rationale if no control group was used; distinguish negative and positive controls and when controls are unnecessary (e.g. within-subject designs, pilot feasibility studies). For complex designs, include a visual representation (timeline or flow chart) showing treatments/procedures and timing, and indicate whether factors are crossed or nested, blocking, or repeated measures. Clearly report all groups used and avoid selectively excluding groups. State if the same control group was used across experiments. See Experimental Design Assistant for diagram support. (Includes subitems 1a: groups/comparators and 1b: definition and justification of the experimental unit; warns about pseudoreplication and gives examples.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample size
rubrics_metrics.description: Report the exact number of experimental units allocated to each group and the total number in each experiment; explain how the sample size was decided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide exact n per group and total animals used; if experimental unit differs from animal, also report total animals. If an a priori power/sample size calculation was used, report analysis method, effect size of interest with justification, estimate of variability and how it was obtained, chosen power and significance threshold, and directionality (one- vs two-sided). Explain when sample size calculations are inappropriate (e.g. production of biological material, pilot/feasibility studies) and justify alternate approaches. Consider anticipated attrition/exclusions when deciding sample size. Provide information sources and recommend consulting a statistician for complex designs. (Covers subitems 2a and 2b; includes parameters used in power calculations and examples.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe any criteria used for including or excluding animals/experimental units during the experiment and data points during analysis, specify whether criteria were established a priori, and report any exclusions and their reasons and the exact n analysed per group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define inclusion/exclusion criteria before data collection; distinguish these from animal characteristics. Describe exclusion criteria arising from technical/welfare issues, quality control failures, or predefined humane endpoints. Explain how outliers and missing data will be handled and whether criteria were pre-specified or pre-registered. Report all exclusions and attrition with reasons (ideally in a table or flowchart), indicate whether those making exclusion decisions were blinded to group allocation, and state the exact n used in each analysis and for each outcome (report absolute numbers, e.g., 10/20). Warn against inappropriate data cleaning and pseudoreplication. (Covers 3a, 3b, 3c; includes examples and rationale.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Randomisation
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe whether and how animals/experimental units were allocated to control and treatment groups to reduce allocation bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report methods used to generate the random allocation sequence and any details of blocking, stratification, or minimisation. Explain procedures used to conceal allocation and to balance known nuisance variables; describe the unit of randomisation. If randomisation was not used, state the rationale. Provide sufficient detail to allow assessment of selection bias and reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blinding
rubrics_metrics.description: Report who was blinded (e.g., caregivers, outcome assessors, data analysts) and at which stages (allocation, conduct, outcome assessment, analysis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State whether personnel were blinded to group allocation during allocation, intervention administration, outcome assessment, and data analysis. If blinding was not possible, explicitly state this and provide justification and any steps taken to minimise bias. Indicate whether blinding was maintained when excluding animals or data points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly define all outcome measures used, specifying primary outcome(s) for hypothesis-testing studies and how and when outcomes were measured.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the primary outcome measure used to determine sample size and the main experimental question. Provide operational definitions, units, measurement techniques, time points and any composite outcomes. Explain how outcomes were chosen and measured and include details to enable replication (e.g., equipment, scoring systems).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe statistical methods used for each analysis, including the experimental unit for each test, how assumptions were assessed, and software used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify the statistical tests, modelling approaches, handling of covariates and nuisance variables, methods used for multiple comparisons, criteria for inclusion/exclusion of data in analyses, treatment of missing data (e.g., imputation), and how outliers were handled. Report measures of precision (e.g., confidence intervals) and effect sizes. State software packages and versions used. For complex designs, justify chosen methods and consider consulting a statistician.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental animals
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide detailed information on the animals used: species, strain, substrain, sex, age or developmental stage, weight, provenance, genetic status, and health/immune status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report source/vendor, breeding/genetic background, any genetic modifications, microbiological status, and details that could affect results. Describe husbandry-related variables relevant to animals (e.g., prior treatments, re-use of animals). This information helps interpret generalisability and reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Give precise details of all experimental procedures, including what was done, how, when, where, and by whom, so the methods can be replicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe interventions, dosing (route, vehicle, volume, concentration), surgical procedures, anaesthesia and analgesia, euthanasia methods, timing relative to measurements, equipment and settings, and any acclimatisation or training. Include welfare-related actions and any unexpected events or protocol deviations. Provide sufficient detail so another laboratory could repeat the procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results
rubrics_metrics.description: Report the findings for each experiment with appropriate summary data, effect sizes and measures of precision, including numbers analysed and any adverse events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present baseline characteristics and outcomes for each group, absolute numbers (n) analysed per outcome, and reasons for any missing data. Report effect sizes with confidence intervals and exact p-values rather than threshold statements. Describe adverse events or harms experienced by animals. Use tables/figures (and flowcharts) to document attrition and numbers at each stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an accurate and informative summary of the study in the abstract, including objectives, key methods, principal findings and conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include essential design elements, species/strain, sample sizes, primary outcome(s) and key quantitative results. The abstract should not overstate conclusions and should reflect limitations where relevant. Use structured abstracts if required by the journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Background
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain scientific background and rationale for the study, placing it in the context of existing evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarise relevant literature, provide justification for the experimental approach and animal model chosen, and explain how the work addresses a gap or question. Avoid overstating the expected importance of results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: State the specific objectives, hypotheses or pre-specified primary and secondary outcomes of the study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly articulate the main research question and any hypotheses being tested. Distinguish confirmatory from exploratory analyses and identify the primary outcome for sample size justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide information on ethical review and licensing, including the relevant approving body and protocol identifiers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State that procedures were approved by an institutional or national ethics committee, provide license/approval numbers where applicable, and describe adherence to relevant guidelines or legislation. Include justification for species/number used with reference to harm–benefit considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Housing and husbandry
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe housing, husbandry and environmental conditions that might influence the animals or study outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report details such as housing type, bedding, social housing (group or single), light/dark cycle, temperature and humidity ranges, diet (type, ad libitum or restricted), water provision, enrichment, and any specialized housing or transport. These factors can affect physiology and behaviour and are important for reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animal care and monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Report monitoring, welfare assessments, and actions taken to minimise pain, suffering and distress before, during and after procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe humane endpoints, monitoring frequency, criteria for euthanasia, use of analgesics or anaesthetics (including doses and timing), veterinary interventions, and any unexpected welfare issues. Report whether animals were monitored blinded to treatment group when welfare decisions were made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation/scientific implications
rubrics_metrics.description: Interpret results in the context of objectives and existing knowledge, acknowledging limitations and alternative explanations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss the biological and scientific significance of findings, consider sources of bias or confounding, reflect on limitations of the model and experiments, and avoid overstating translational potential. Suggest next steps and how findings fit into the broader field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generalisability/translation
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss the extent to which results are generalisable beyond the study conditions and implications for translation to other species or humans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider species, strain, sex, age, laboratory conditions, and model limitations when discussing external validity. Be cautious about extrapolating to humans; report factors that support or limit translatability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protocol registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Report whether the study protocol, hypotheses and analysis plan were pre-registered and where the protocol can be accessed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide links or identifiers for registered protocols (e.g., OSF, clinical trial registries), and indicate deviations from the registered plan with justification. Pre-registration is encouraged to limit selective reporting and analytic flexibility; include registered primary outcomes and analysis plans when available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data access
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a statement describing whether and where study data are available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State if data and associated metadata are made publicly available and provide repository names/links/DOIs. Follow FAIR principles (findable, accessible, interoperable, reusable). Recommend domain-specific repositories (NCBI, EBI) or general repositories (Figshare, Dryad, Zenodo, OSF) and cite data availability examples. Explain any restrictions on access and how to obtain data if not publicly available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaration of interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Declare any potential conflicts of interest (financial and non-financial) and list all funding sources and the role of funders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report financial and non-financial competing interests (including employment, advisory roles, intellectual property, personal relationships, ideological positions). If none exist, state this explicitly. Provide full funding details including grant identifiers and state the funder's role in study design, data collection, analysis, reporting, and decision to publish; if research was performed as part of employment, name the employer.
